description: Which items are about to run out? Ranks items ascending by daysOnHand (current available ÷ the planning rate — the stockout-urgency signal), so the most urgent are first. Filters (all optional): minDays / maxDays bound daysOnHand; includeNoConsumption (default false) excludes items with no demand signal (null daysOnHand) unless set true. Each row also carries aggregatedInventoryDays (including inbound POs + buildable capacity — the procurement-planning view) and a velocity-confidence tier. Available is live stock before units committed to open orders, the figure the days-on-hand math uses: the planning rate already counts those orders as demand. For available net of committed units, as the Inventory page and Shopify show it, use list_items or get_item_stock_outlook. Paged by limit (default 50, max 200); TotalMatching is the pre-paging count. A client-pinned token sees only its own client's items.

includeNoConsumption.description: Include items with no demand signal (null daysOnHand); default false excludes them.

maxDays.description: Only items with daysOnHand on/below this value.

minDays.description: Only items with daysOnHand on/above this value.

name: get_items_by_days_of_supply

aggregatedInventoryDays.description: Effective inventory (including inbound POs and buildable capacity) ÷ the planning rate: the procurement-planning signal. Null means no demand signal.

dailyConsumption.description: Planning rate, units/day (dailyConsumption): what the warehouse plans stock for. The higher of the forecast and the sales rate (plus sales with no order behind them), raised by scheduled production and BOM pulls; at a warehouse that supplies transfer nodes it includes what they pull. Conservative on purpose. Days on hand divides by this rate.

daysOnHand.description: Available ÷ the planning rate (dailyConsumption): the stockout-urgency signal this tool ranks on. Null means no demand signal.

title: Items by Days of Supply
